Southwest's 2025 fuel-hedge exit did not end the expense clock




Why it matters: Southwest Airlines Co.'s filing tied later premium expense to the originally forecast transactions, even after closure removed the hedge assets. Capital Chronicle's analysis is that an accounting tail can outlive the portfolio.




Context: Southwest Airlines Co.'s disclosure explains accounting timing; deferred expense is not a verdict on whether the hedge exit was economically sound. The passage does not measure the contracts' overall benefit or establish how the exit changed subsequent earnings.
